An oversized paragraph is split at line boundaries, then sentences, then runes as a last resort, with no text lost.
A small final tail chunk below Budget.MinTail tokens is merged back into the previous chunk.
A chunk's Context is the tail of the previous chunk's text cut at a line start; the first chunk has empty Context.
ChunkText splits plain text only on blank lines, does not treat # lines as headings, and gives chunks an empty HeadingPath.
Chunk Index values must be sequential from 0 in every case. The no-loss and no-duplication check, ignoring whitespace, applies only to cases flagged noLoss.

stored.fact: internal/llmprompts holds every LLM prompt and LLM-facing instruction that both apps send; it is distinct from internal/prompts, the P246 popup router.
registry.go is the only file containing prompt text; each entry has id, kind, apps, catalog keys, applies-when, default, required fragments and a fixed output schema.
User-authored text (smart-script bodies, workflow stage and step prompts), tool and server names, tool error strings and result data formatting are not in the prompt registry.
Prompt kinds are system, message, suffix, instructions, tool, argument, toolResult and fragment; fragments are included via {{template}}.
Argument prompt entries describe one MCP tool property and carry Parent tool and Field.
InputSchema[T] sets each tool property's description from its argument entry; a mismatch panics at server build, and jsonschema tags are not used.
Prompt templates use text/template with only the funcs inc and join; an entry with NoVars and no fragments is literal and never parsed.
Default prompts render byte-identical to the pre-P271 output, verified against testdata/golden.

Prompt overrides are stored per app in <home>/llm-prompts.json (~/.kira-studio/, ~/.kira-space/), written with renameio at mode 0600; saving the default text removes the override; override text must be 1 byte to 32 KiB.
A prompt change carries baseHash and a stale one is refused with E_CONFLICT.

If the prompt store file is corrupt or an override no longer validates, the default is used, a warning is logged and it is flagged in Settings; defaultChanged flags an override made against an older default.

Server-side validation of prompt overrides requires the template to parse, every prompt:"required" variable to be referenced, every required fragment to be included, and execution against example vars to succeed.
The memory system prompts must include the memory.dataHygiene fragment, which provides injection defence.
Schema-bound prompts (gate, reconcile, import extract and finalize) keep their JSON schema fixed, shown read-only in Settings.
There is no global prompt source; consumers receive a llmprompts.Source (Resolve, Revision) through their options, and Defaults() is the registry-only source.
Store.Resolve stats the file on every call and re-reads it when mtime or size changes.
Gate, reconcile, import, headless suffixes and ADE messages resolve prompts per call, so an edit applies on the next call.
memory-mcp (stdio subprocess) builds instructions and tool/argument descriptions once per process, so edits apply only to new Claude sessions.
dbmcp and claudeheadless rebuild MCP servers when Revision() changes.
LlmPromptsService (List, Save, Preview) exists in both apps and emits event kira:llmPrompts:changed with {revision}; Save is all-or-nothing, with per-id errors returned as an E_BAD_REQUEST payload.
Preview with real vars also renders the ADE run dialog and step inspector, so no TypeScript copy of a prompt exists.

Settings has a Prompts section before Advanced in both apps, with a list, Monaco editor, diff against default, Preview and per-entry reset; drafts live in Pinia store llmPromptDrafts, and dialog Save saves prompts before the settings patch.

The guard go run ./internal/llmprompts/cmd/checkprompts, part of bun run lint, fails on jsonschema tags, MCP Description/Instructions or memory.Call System not sourced from llmprompts, and on copies of registry defaults outside internal/llmprompts and internal/flowtest.
